source_name: NEN — Národní elektronický nástroj (National Electronic Tool for e-procurement)
why_relevant: Central Czech e-procurement platform where a large share of state bodies run tenders end-to-end. Detail pages carry zadávací dokumentace, estimated value, CPV, and the awarded supplier. Confirmed to contain banking/payment-relevant procedures, e.g. payment-gateway services for ČTÚ (N006-24-V00022811), a Dynamic Purchasing System for payment gateways for public administration run by Ministry of Interior (N006-20-V00032360), and card-acceptance/terminal rental tenders (N006-24-V00003391).

source_name: Věstník veřejných zakázek (VVZ) — Czech public contracts bulletin
why_relevant: Statutory single point where contracting authorities publish contract notices AND 'Oznámení o výsledku zadávacího řízení' (award notices) under Act 134/2016 Sb. Award forms name the winning supplier and the contract value — the canonical evidence layer for who won which core banking / card / payment system contract.

source_name: Registr smluv (ISRS) — Czech contract register
source_subtype: statutory contract register with full documents
why_relevant: Under Act 340/2015 Sb. every contract above CZK 50k concluded by a mandatory public body must be published, with the full contract text attached, within 30 days — otherwise it is void. This is the single richest legal-disclosure channel for actual vendor names, contract value, duration and often full SLA/scope PDFs for banking, card and payment systems. Administered by DIA since 2023.

source_name: Registr smluv open dataset in NKOD (Národní katalog otevřených dat)
why_relevant: Machine-readable distribution of the contract register — the practical ingestion path for longitudinal vendor/contract-value tracking without scraping.

source_name: Portál o veřejných zakázkách (portal-vz.cz) — MMR methodology & NIPEZ hub
why_relevant: Official hub explaining how NIPEZ / VVZ / profily zadavatele / NEN interlock, which forms exist and what must be published where. Essential to design a complete crawl and to know what evidence is legally guaranteed to exist. Also hosts annual state-of-procurement reports and a decisions database.

source_name: E-ZAK ČNB — Czech National Bank contracting-authority profile
why_relevant: ČNB is the central bank and the single most strategically relevant Czech public buyer of banking/payment IT (CERTIS, cash handling, card acquiring for own operations, core IT). Its profil zadavatele carries below-threshold and small-scale contracts that never reach VVZ. IČO 48136450, VVZ profile ID 342165.

source_name: ČNB — Veřejné zakázky (official procurement landing page)
why_relevant: Authoritative pointer from ČNB to all channels it uses (E-ZAK profile, Gemin e-marketplace), plus its internal thresholds — tells you which contract sizes will and will not be visible where.

source_name: Gemin — elektronické tržiště (e-marketplace), ČNB profile
why_relevant: One of the certified Czech e-marketplaces used for small-scale and below-threshold purchases. ČNB explicitly routes procurement here, so it captures the long tail of banking-IT spend (licences, support, integration work) invisible in VVZ.

source_name: Tender arena — profil zadavatele platform (Česká pošta, EGAP, Národní rozvojová banka)
why_relevant: Hosts contracting-authority profiles for several high-value banking/payments-adjacent state bodies: Česká pošta s.p. (profile Z0002718 — postal payment/cash services, Czech POINT, large IT), EGAP (export credit insurer) and Národní rozvojová banka (state development bank, ex-ČMZRB). These are exactly the state-owned financial institutions that buy core/payment systems.

source_name: Česká pošta, s.p. — Veřejné zakázky
why_relevant: Czech Post operates postal payment orders, cash services, Czech POINT and (historically) Poštovní spořitelna-linked counters; it is a major buyer of payment/terminal/counter systems. Page routes to its Tender arena profile.

source_name: EGAP — Veřejné zakázky (Export Guarantee and Insurance Company)
why_relevant: State export-credit insurer; a financial institution whose core insurance/underwriting and payment IT procurement is legally disclosed. Publishes via Tender arena profile.

source_name: Národní rozvojová banka, a.s. — profil zadavatele (Tender arena)
why_relevant: State development bank (formerly ČMZRB) — a real bank subject to procurement law, therefore its core banking / loan-origination / payment infrastructure purchases are publicly disclosed. Rare and high-value evidence of a Czech bank's vendor stack.

source_name: Ministerstvo financí ČR — Profil zadavatele
why_relevant: MF owns state treasury/payment infrastructure (Státní pokladna, IISSP), tax payment channels and centrally coordinated purchasing (společný nákup) for the resort — a major source of payment-systems contracts and of vendor framework agreements.

source_name: Hlídač státu — Hlídač veřejných zakázek & Hlídač smluv (+ public API)
why_relevant: NGO aggregator that normalises Registr smluv, VVZ/procurement, subsidies and ÚOHS decisions into one searchable, API-accessible corpus. Supports field prefixes icoDodavatel:, icoZadavatel:, cpv: — which makes vendor-level and CPV-level longitudinal analysis practical without building your own ETL. Best single entry point for competitor/vendor mapping.

source_name: RegistrySmluv.cz — alternative contract-register search front-end
why_relevant: Independent search interface over the same statutory contract data; useful as a redundancy path and sometimes for better full-text search of contract subjects than the official UI.

source_name: vhodne-uverejneni.cz — profil zadavatele platform and procurement explainers
why_relevant: Another multi-tenant profil zadavatele host (e.g. it carries a ČNB profile page under IČO 48136450 and a Česká pošta profile). Also publishes practical explainers on what VVZ vs profil zadavatele vs e-tržiště each contain — useful for coverage design.

source_name: E-ZAKAZKY.CZ — profil zadavatele platform
why_relevant: Third major commercial e-tool hosting Czech contracting-authority profiles. Needed for full coverage because Czech authorities are split across NEN, E-ZAK instances, Tender arena, Gemin, vhodné uveřejnění and E-ZAKAZKY.

source_name: ÚOHS — Sbírky rozhodnutí (antitrust/procurement-review decisions)
why_relevant: Procurement-review decisions expose things tender notices hide: which vendors bid and lost, who challenged whom, disputed technical specifications, allegations of vendor lock-in in core banking/IT. ÚOHS even publishes a periodically updated compendium of selected IT-procurement decisions. High-value competitor-intelligence layer.

source_name: Portál gov.cz — Registr smluv service page (publication mechanics)
why_relevant: Explains the publication workflow, metadata schema and legal exemptions — needed to know what is systematically missing (e.g. contracts exempt from disclosure) before drawing coverage conclusions.

source_name: NKOD / data.gov.cz — national open data catalogue (dataset discovery)
why_relevant: Master index for machine-readable versions of every mandatory public register relevant here (Registr smluv, ÚOHS decisions, and procurement-related datasets), with DCAT distributions and open formal standards. The right place to discover new structured feeds instead of scraping.

source_name: Ministry of Interior DNS for public-administration payment gateways (NEN N006-20-V00032360)
why_relevant: A live Dynamic Purchasing System means an enumerable, continuously updated list of QUALIFIED payment-gateway suppliers to the Czech state, plus each mini-tender award. Effectively a public competitor register for the CZ public-sector payment-gateway market — one of the highest-value single objects in this cell.

source_name: TED — Tenders Electronic Daily (EU procurement notices, Czech-language interface)
why_relevant: Primary EU-level publication venue for all above-threshold Czech contract notices and award notices. Notices are structured (eForms XML), carry CPV codes, buyer identity (ICO), estimated/awarded value and, critically for A6, the WINNING SUPPLIER name and any consortium members — which is the single most direct evidence of which vendors (Diebold Nixdorf, NCR Atleos, Worldline, Nexi, Temenos, Fiserv, Monet+, ICZ, Asseco Central Europe) are winning Czech banking/payments work. Multilingual rendering means Czech-only notices become readable in EN.

source_name: TED API (search + bulk notice retrieval)
why_relevant: Machine-readable access to the same notice corpus, enabling standing queries (country=CZ, CPV in banking/payments set, notice-type=award) instead of manual searching. This is the recommended long-term collection channel for this cell: it returns structured supplier names and values that can be diffed run-over-run to detect new vendor entries into the Czech market.

source_name: TED XML bulk download (daily/monthly notice archives)
why_relevant: Full historical corpus of notices as XML archives. Enables retrospective build of a Czech banking/payments contract history (who won what, when, at what value) rather than only forward monitoring — the basis for competitor share-of-wins analysis and for finding case-study-worthy reference projects.

source_name: eForms SDK / eForms metadata reference (TED Developer Docs)
why_relevant: Defines the field schema of modern TED notices (business terms BT-xxx: winner name, winner national ID, contract value, subcontracting, framework agreement flags). Without this the structured notices cannot be parsed reliably. It is also a pointer to which intelligence attributes are actually available per notice — e.g. whether subcontractors and consortium partners are disclosed, which matters for mapping partnerships.

source_name: data.europa.eu — TED dataset (CSV/RDF derivatives of EU procurement notices)
why_relevant: Pre-flattened, analysis-ready extracts of TED notices published on the official EU open data portal, with a Czech-language landing page. Lower-friction than the API for trend analysis (award counts and values by CPV and by supplier country), and useful as a cross-check that the API-based collection is complete.

source_name: CPV (Common Procurement Vocabulary) taxonomy as a discovery pointer
why_relevant: The CPV code list is itself an intelligence asset: choosing the right code set (e.g. 72212443 banking software development, 48xxxxxx software packages, 30123600 coin-handling/cash devices family, 66xxxxxx financial services, 72xxxxxx IT services, 50xxxxxx repair & maintenance) determines whether an entire class of Czech banking/payments contracts is seen or missed. Codes also let one enumerate adjacent contract classes not on any prior checklist.

source_name: EU Funding & Tenders Portal (SEDIA) — calls, tenders and project results
why_relevant: Single entry point for EU-managed funding and Commission procurement. Its 'Projects & results' section names Czech beneficiaries and consortium partners in digitalisation projects — directly revealing partnerships and reference projects (case studies) involving Czech banks, fintechs and IT integrators that never surface in national procurement.
